title: A diacylglycerol photoswitching protocol for studying TRPC channel functions in mammalian cells and tissue slices
protocol: Produce patch pipettes made of borosilicate glass with resistances of 2.0–3.5 MΩ (HEK293T cells) or 5–8 MΩ (olfactory neurons) for whole-cell measurements.
Place the slice in a perfusion chamber of the electrophysiology microscope.
Perfuse the cells/slice with bath solution S1 (aerated with 95% O2 / 5% CO2) or S3 (HEK293T cells).
Control the flow rate of the bath perfusion solution using a pump or gravity feed.
Maintain strict control over the solution speed in a gravity feed system using volume and gravity flow controllers.
Keep track of the perfusion solution volume to maintain equal pressure on the tubing lines.
Mount glass bottom dishes with loaded cells onto the stage of the inverse microscope for TRPC6 channel activity measurements in transfected HEK293T cells.
Fill the recording electrode with artificial intracellular solution (S4 or S5).
Place the filled recording electrode in the pipette holder of the amplifier headstage.
Apply positive pressure using a syringe to prevent air bubbles and debris attachment during electrode transfer into the bath solution.
Set the amplifier according to the manufacturer’s manual.
Apply a test pulse to monitor the pipette/seal resistance.
Bring the recording electrode into the bath solution.
Monitor and correct your junction potential between the solutions.
Approach the cell of interest slowly.
Form a gigaseal between the cell membrane and recording pipette electrode by releasing positive pressure and applying suction.
Change the voltage to the predicted resting potential of the cell (−60 mV for most neurons).
Correct for fast capacitance.
Rupture the cell membrane under the electrode by introducing sudden low pressure.
Obtain families of whole-cell currents to a series of depolarizing and hyperpolarizing voltage steps in complete darkness.
Obtain families of whole-cell currents during activating and inactivating photoswitching illuminations.
Keep VSNs at a holding potential of −70 mV before initiating a cycle of step protocols.
Set the monochromator to fluorescence light of λ = 350 or 360 nm and λ = 450 nm with maximal intensity (100%) using PolyCon 3.2 software.
Use fiber-coupled LEDs with nominal wavelengths of λ = 365 nm (4.1 mW) for activating PhoDAG and λ = 470 nm (10.1 mW) for deactivating PhoDAG in patch-clamp experiments.
Directly couple a bifurcated fiber bundle with a 400 μm core to the LEDs.
Align a 400-μm thick optical fiber with a thinner optical fiber (200 μm, 0.22 NA) placed directly in the bath solution in front of cell preparations.
Control light switching using a DC4104 LED controller with a 1-ms switching time triggered by a TTL signal controlled by the patch-clamp amplifier.
Analyze the data using Igor Pro, Origin, or similar software packages.
Acquire current-voltage (I-V) curves by applying a series of depolarizing and hyperpolarizing voltage steps.
Acquire I-V curves by applying voltage-ramp protocols.
Derive reversal potential from I-V curves.
Determine ionic properties and selectivity from I-V curves.
Identify voltage-dependence and rectification of I-V curves.
Establish activation threshold from I-V curves.
Evaluate overall conductance properties.
Use fitting routines in Igor Pro to determine activation time constants.
Use fitting routines in Igor Pro to determine inactivation time constants.
Use fitting routines in Igor Pro to determine deactivation time constants.
Apply the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm to minimize least squared errors.
Preincubate an untransfected HEK293T cell with 30 μM OptoDArG.
Plot data points from ramp currents of the preincubated cell at 100 and -100 mV versus time.
Expose the cell to 360 nm UV light to test for current induction.
Record a representative time course of a light-evoked hTRPC6 current at a holding potential of -60 mV.
Illuminate the cell using light with wavelengths λ = 360 nm or λ = 450 nm as depicted in the protocol.
Dilute the 100 mM PhoDAG-1 stock solution to a final concentration of 100 μM PhoDAG-1 if necessary for infusion through the patch pipette.
Place dissociated cells or tissue slices co-loaded with a calcium indicator and PhoDAG in a laminar flow recording chamber.
Continuously perfuse the recording chamber with extracellular S1 solution aerated with 95% O2 / 5% CO2 at an appropriate flow rate (e.g., 100 μL/s).
Control the flow of the bath perfusion solution using a pump or gravity feed.
Visualize the cells within a scanning field of 512 x 512 pixels and a depth of ∼9 μm.
Adjust the pixel dwell time of the laser to a total image scanning of ∼1 s.
Perform calcium fluorescence imaging of the cells/tissue using an Argon laser with an excitation wavelength of 488 nm for 4 minutes.
Capture the emission fluorescence between 510 and 560 nm using Zen software (Zeiss).
Use UV light at a wavelength of 355 nm to scan preselected regions-of-interests via the Zen software tool ‘Bleaching’ for photoswitching PhoDAG compounds to the active cis form.
Activate the pre-installed shutter via the Zen software protocol to block UV light from reaching the gallium-arsenide-phosphide (GaAsP) detectors during imaging.
Analyze images using Zen software from Zeiss.
Mark regions-of-interests (ROIs) for analysis using Zen or ImageJ software.
Export raw fluorescence intensity of ROIs versus time to an analysis program like Igor Pro.
Determine average baseline fluorescence values (Fo) in Igor Pro.
Calculate cytosolic changes in fluorescence intensity as (F–Fo)/Fo.
Define onset time of Ca2+ transients as the difference between 488 nm excitation start and when Ca2+ fluorescence exceeds twice the standard deviation of baseline noise.
Determine other parameters such as Fpeak, activation, and deactivation time courses using Igor Pro tools.
